prerequisites: It is recommended not to take this course until having achieved as complete a vision as possible of the technical disciplines taught in the degree.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Organization Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to organize and plan in the field of business, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the field of Industrial Organization Engineering.
Ability to prevent occupational risks and protect the health and safety of workers and users.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Knowledge and abilities to organize and manage projects. Understand the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Understand the requirements and legal and ethical implications of professional engineering practice, particularly in project development.
Know the characteristics of projects, their life cycle and the technical, economic, safety, environmental, legal, social and ethical conditions to consider in them.

Define the scope of a project and plan the deadlines and costs of all necessary tasks to carry it out, and carry out progress control and supervision of the work to be performed in a project, keeping the initial planning in mind.
Clearly explain and adequately justify the solutions adopted in a project, preparing the associated documents that allow its contracting and execution.
Know the structure and functions of a technical office, as well as elaborate and improve a work method.

syllabus_topics: Topic 6: Regulatory framework and Project Processing.
teaching_methods: Computer lab practices (planning, budgeting, graphic tools, document management)
assessment_rules: To pass in the ordinary call, it is mandatory to obtain a minimum of 5 points out of 10 in each of the three parts (EV-1, EV-2, EV-3). If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as: Note = 0.4 * EV-1 + 0.35 * EV-2 + 0.25 * EV-3. Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0. For EV-2, the average of two individual assignments is taken, provided each is > 4.0; otherwise, the score is min(average, 4.0). For EV-3, in the ordinary call, it's 0.5 * (exercises performed in class) + 0.5 * (Laboratory Practices exam); in the extraordinary call, it's solely the Laboratory Practices exam. In the extraordinary call, scores > 5 from the ordinary call can be carried over. For differentiated evaluation, attendance to practices is not compulsory, and EV-3 is calculated as 0.25 * (grade for exercises performed) + 0.75 * (Laboratory Practices exam grade) for the ordinary call, and solely the Laboratory Practices exam grade for the extraordinary call.
